title: RAW UNREVIEWED: Vitruvius lamp test: failed air observation changes the permitted descent and triggers ventilation
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED_NOT_SELECTED_NOT_TESTED. The source links dangerous well exhalations to a lowered lamp: continued burning permits descent, extinction calls for adjacent air shafts before proceeding. An instrument outcome controls permission for a later human action, and a failed outcome prescribes an environmental intervention. This distinguishes diagnosis, advice and achieved safety.

source.observed_content: The source links dangerous well exhalations to a lowered lamp: continued burning permits descent, extinction calls for adjacent air shafts before proceeding.
source.layer: Modern edition/translation of an ancient primary work; source-only exploratory input, not a newly collated medieval witness

potential_admitted_target: An already-admitted body/bath panel such as f77r is only a potential full-record target; a drawn basin is not itself a well or a lamp.

design.mechanism: An instrument outcome controls permission for a later human action, and a failed outcome prescribes an environmental intervention. This distinguishes diagnosis, advice and achieved safety.
design.unit: Both complete source paragraphs and one target unit with instrument, observation, descent and ventilation owners.
design.contrast: A direct treatment account makes the lamp or air shaft heal the person. A purely descriptive air-quality list does not condition descent. The source does not provide an explicit post-ventilation repeat lamp measurement.
design.prediction: The target should retain observation-before-decision and failed-test-before-intervention, while not asserting a repeat test or guaranteed safe outcome that the source omits.
design.scope: Source-only raw proposal; no selected manuscript content, assigned glosses or executed experiment

execution_requirements: Find a dated illustrated primary with lamp and well/shaft owners or a complete owned textual counterpart; a generic fire/water image is insufficient.
Check whether an already-admitted target actually has capacity for both observation and intervention; keep absent roles explicit.
Write conditional attachment and participant reuse across the complete paragraph; retain GDT818 repeated-form and attachment countercases.
assumptions_and_limits: No Voynich word receives a meaning from this proposal.
An ancient work in a modern edition supplies historical content, not a medieval manuscript owner or independent Voynich binding.
The named target is a potential already-admitted locus, not a claim that its image or text contains the required roles. Root must verify the exact admission and ownership before selection.
